name: rbi_policy_reaction_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: RBI monetary policy announcements (6 per year, typically at 10:00 IST) create a predictable intraday pattern: (1) pre-announcement compression (09:15-10:00) where volatility drops and prices consolidate, (2) knee-jerk reaction (10:00-10:15) where BANK NIFTY moves 50-200 bps in the direction of the surprise, (3) partial reversal (10:15-10:45) as the initial reaction overshoots, (4) trend resumption (10:45-12:00) as the market digests the full statement. The strategy trades phase 3 (fade the overshoot) and phase 4 (follow the trend). The inefficiency exists because retail traders react emotionally to headlines ('rate cut!' or 'hawkish hold!') without reading the statement, creating an overshoot that sophisticated participants fade. The phase 4 trend is driven by institutional portfolio adjustments.
mechanism: RBI policy announcements create predictable pre-announcement compression and post-announcement expansion. Before the announcement, participants reduce positions, compressing volatility. After the announcement, directional flow surges as the rate decision is parsed. The initial reaction often overshoots, creating a fading opportunity within 15-30 minutes.

conditions: PHASE 3 (10:15-10:45): banknifty_reaction < -50 bps (sold off on hawkish surprise) AND retracement_pct > 0.3 (already started bouncing)
OR PHASE 4 (10:45-12:00): banknifty_reaction > 0 (dovish surprise) AND close > VWAP AND gilt_yield_change < -3 bps (yields confirming dovishness)
PHASE 3: banknifty_reaction > 50 bps (rallied on dovish surprise) AND retracement_pct > 0.3
OR PHASE 4: banknifty_reaction < 0 (hawkish surprise) AND close < VWAP AND gilt_yield_change > 3 bps

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (VIX spike is part of the signal, not a filter)
filters.volume_filter: BANK NIFTY volume > 1.5x normal on policy day (confirmed interest)

weaknesses: Only 6 trade days per year (RBI policy meetings) — the strategy cannot be a primary income source and contributes minimally to annual P&L.
The Phase 3/Phase 4 framework assumes a standard reaction pattern, but emergency meetings or coordinated global central bank actions create non-standard patterns.
Slippage on RBI policy days is significantly higher than normal — the 3 bps assumption is optimistic; actual slippage may be 5-10 bps during peak reaction.
prior_art: Lucca & Moench (2015) 'The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift' — the Fed equivalent of this strategy. Bernanke & Kuttner (2005) 'What Explains the Stock Market's Reaction to Federal Reserve Policy?'. In India, Patel (2017) studies RBI rate decision impact on banking stocks.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to BANKNIFTY index.
